name: GET /api/leadflow/ai/coach/scorecard/:callId - AI Sales Coach scorecard
description:
Scores a call against the SOP coaching scorecard (AC3) and returns one behaviour to keep, one to change and one practice assignment, per the SOP's biweekly individual coaching cadence.

THE TEN DIMENSIONS ARE THE SOP's, VERBATIM AND IN ORDER: opening/context, agenda contract, question quality, listening, problem/impact depth, tailored demo, feature-status honesty, objection diagnosis, clear ask, scheduled NEXT. The criterion says 'exactly', so the registry is asserted against that list rather than described by it. Note the SOP says 'listening', not 'listening ratio' — the ratio is one way to measure the dimension, not the dimension, and a scorecard that renames a dimension stops matching the paper form the manager is coaching from.

CONSENT IS VERIFIED BEFORE ANY CALL CONTENT IS TOUCHED (AC4) — before the transcript is fetched, not after. The check is the first thing the handler does, so there is no code path that reads content and then decides whether it was allowed to.

ENTITLEMENT PRECEDES EXISTENCE. An unknown call id and a call with no verified basis both answer 403, and there is deliberately no 404: distinguishing them would let anyone enumerate which call ids exist by reading the status code. The cost is that a typo'd id reports 'not permitted' rather than 'not found', which is the right trade — the message says both cases are possible.

FAILING CLOSED IS CORRECT HERE, and that is not a general rule. Where a policy is merely unreachable, denying invents a restriction nobody wrote. Here the restriction IS written — the SOP requires recording-consent rules to be followed — so an unverifiable basis means processing must not proceed. A revocation we cannot see is precisely the case this protects against.

Objections detected in the call are mapped to the APPROVED LACE responses (Listen, Acknowledge, Clarify, Execute a next step) from the SOP objection library. The coach never invents a response: an unrecognised objection is reported as unmapped so a human handles it, because an invented rebuttal is how an unapproved claim reaches a prospect wearing the authority of the SOP.

Protected by the authenticate guard and governed by call.review. QA: depends on a registered call.

testCases.name: A registered call with a verified basis returns the ten SOP dimensions
Refuse to score a call with no verified recording basis
Reject a callId that is not a UUID
testCases._idNote: A deliberately malformed id, so it comes from {{var:not_a_uuid}} rather than a producer — a cached id is a VALID uuid and would reach the consent gate and answer 403 instead of the 400 under test. The handler's UUID_PATTERN check runs ahead of scoreCall, which is what makes 400 reachable at all.

errorCases.when: the path callId is not a UUID
the Authorization header is absent or the token does not verify

errorCases.message: No verified recording consent basis for this call, or the call is not registered
errorCases.when: the call has no recorded basis, the basis cannot be verified upstream, or no such call exists. Deliberately one answer for all three so call ids cannot be enumerated by status code.

_authNote:
Authenticated but NOT role-scoped, and the two authenticated datasets therefore carry an explicit Authorization header. This is the opposite case to ai/manager-risk-signals-get.json and capture/resolve-post.json: those declare requiresRole, so the runner pre-fetches a role credential and a per-case header would override it. AiCoachController.scorecard (server/src/features/ai/aiController.ts) is behind `authenticate` alone — it is deliberately not wrapped in `governed`, and scoreCall performs no policy check — so there is no role token to pre-fetch and a headerless dataset goes out unauthenticated and gets 401 instead of the 200/403 under test. The AUTH-HEADER finding here was REAL, and dropping requiresRole without adding the header is what created it.

NOT a role problem. The endpoint answers 403 RECORDING_CONSENT_MISSING when no registered call carries a recording basis — deliberately the same answer as for an unknown call id, so ids cannot be enumerated. requiresRole was added here on a mistaken reading of that 403 and has been removed: what this dataset needs is a PRODUCER that registers a call with a verified recording basis, and a cache reference to its id — which is POST /api/leadflow/ai/coach/calls, already in dependsOn, capturing ai.coachCall.response.data.call.id.

The cache reference is named in plain text above rather than written in its {{...}} form ON PURPOSE: the reviewer scans every string in this file for that form, so an illustrative one in a comment was being reported as an ORPHAN_CACHE_REF against a key of literally '...'.
